blurb: Large white livestock guardian of the Pyrenees, known in the US as the Great Pyrenees
description: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog, or Great Pyrenees, is a large white livestock guardian from the Pyrenees with a long thick double coat and double dewclaws.
answer: The Pyrenean Mountain Dog, called the Patou in France and the Great Pyrenees in the United States, is a large livestock guardian dog from the Pyrenees, the mountains between France and Spain. It is powerfully built, with a long, thick, mostly white double coat, and is still widely used to protect flocks from wolves and bears.

body: Shepherds in the Pyrenees used these dogs for centuries to guard flocks, often fitting them with spiked iron collars against wolves. In the seventeenth century a dog of this type reached the court of Louis XIV, who named it the Royal Dog of France. After wolves disappeared from the Pyrenees the breed nearly died out, until Bernard Senac-Lagrange founded a breed club and wrote the first standard in 1923. The FCI definitively accepted it in 1955. It is closely related to, but separate from, the Pyrenean Mastiff.

Under the Société Centrale Canine standard, dogs stand 70–80 cm and bitches 65–75 cm, and adults typically weigh 55–75 kg. The muzzle is long and broad, the small triangular ears lie flat, and the long tail curls over the back when alert. Double dewclaws on the hind legs are a distinctive feature. The long double coat is mainly white, sometimes with black, badger, grey or tan patches on the head.

The source text gives little detail on temperament. The breed is described above all as a working livestock guardian; some hikers in the Pyrenees have been confronted by dogs protecting their flocks. Breed club descriptions are the best guide to the character of individual dogs.

Sources give little detail on care as a companion. The thick coat provides insulation in harsh mountain weather. The breed continues to work as a flock guardian in the French Pyrenees and Alps and in the United States.

Sources name few specific conditions in the breed. A 2024 UK study reported a median lifespan of 10.9 years, and a Swedish insurance study found that 58% died by age 10. Breed clubs recommend health screening of breeding stock and regular veterinary check-ups.

faq.q: How big does a Pyrenean Mountain Dog get?
faq.a: It is a large breed: dogs stand 70–80 cm and bitches 65–75 cm, with adults typically weighing 55–75 kg.

faq.q: Is the Great Pyrenees the same as the Pyrenean Mountain Dog?
faq.a: Yes. Great Pyrenees is the American name for the Pyrenean Mountain Dog, known in France as the Patou.

faq.q: How long do Pyrenean Mountain Dogs live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study reported a median lifespan of 10.9 years.

faq.q: Is the Pyrenean Mountain Dog recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 137 in Group 2.
